units.summary: Add a global usage text. This is not used by sub-commands.

guarantees.text: adds a global usage text, which is not used by sub-commands
creates and returns a command instance for `name` and `description`
in a command name, angled brackets indicate required arguments and square brackets indicate optional arguments ("deploy <folder>" requires `folder`, "build [project]" makes `project` optional)
only the last argument can be variadic, written with "..." at the start of its name ("build <entry> [...otherFiles]"), and then it is passed as an array
a command name with no name and only brackets ("[...files]") is the default command, used when no other command is matched
`config.allowUnknownOptions` allows unknown options in this command
`config.ignoreOptionDefaultValue` leaves the default value of an option out of the parsed options and only displays it in the help message

units.summary: Add a global CLI option. Which is also applied to sub-commands.

guarantees.text: adds a global option
`config.default` is the default value of the option (`--type <type>` with `default: "node"` defaults `type` to "node")
when `config.type` is `[]`, the option value is an array, and a conversion function such as `[String]` is invoked on the option value
an option in kebab-case is mapped to camelCase, so `--clear-screen` and `--clearScreen` both map to `options.clearScreen`
in an option name, angled brackets indicate that a string or number value is required and square brackets indicate that the value can also be `true`
with `--no-config` and `--config <path>`, the default value of `config` is `true` and the flag `--no-config` sets it to `false`
an option given once gives a single value ("--include project-a" gives `{ include: "project-a" }`) and given twice gives an array (`{ include: ["project-a", "project-b"] }`)

units.summary: Show help message when `-h, --help` flags appear.

guarantees.text: outputs the help message when the `-h` or `--help` flag appears
the optional `callback` receives the help sections, each with an optional `title` and a `body`, so the help text can be post-processed before it is displayed

units.summary: Show version number when `-v, --version` flags appear.

guarantees.text: outputs the version number when the `-v` or `--version` flag appears, because `customFlags` is "-v, --version" by default
`customFlags` replaces the flags that output the version number
the version number is also used in the help message

units.summary: Add a global example. This example added here will not be used by sub-commands.
Output the corresponding help message When a sub-command is matched, output the help message for the command Otherwise output the global one.

guarantees.text: outputs the help message
returns an object with `args`, an array of strings, and `options`, an object of the parsed options
`argv` is `process.argv` by default
after the call, `cli.rawArgs`, `cli.args`, `cli.options` and `cli.matchedCommand` are available
with `{ run: false }` it parses the arguments without running the command, which can then be run with `runMatchedCommand`
runs the matched command after `parse` was called with `{ run: false }`, and its result can be awaited when the command action returns a Promise
adds a usage text for this command
allows unknown options in this command
by default an error is logged when unknown options are used
adds an example which is displayed at the end of the help message
`example` is either a string or a function that takes the command name and returns a string

units.summary: Add a option for this command

guarantees.text: adds the option to this specific command, like `cli.option` does for the CLI ("-r, --recursive" on "rm <dir>" gives `options.recursive`)
`--clear-screen` and `--clearScreen` are both mapped to `options.clearScreen`
adds an alias name to this command
the alias `name` cannot contain brackets
uses the callback as the command action when the command matches the user inputs, called with the parsed CLI args first and the parsed CLI options last
the last argument is an array when it is a variadic argument

units.summary: Check if a command name is matched by this command
Check if an option is registered in this command
Check if the parsed options contain any unknown options Exit and output error when true
Check if the required string-type options exist
Check if the number of args is more than expected

guarantees.text: `cac(name)` creates a CLI instance, and the optional `name` is the program name displayed in the help and version messages
when `name` is not set, the program name is the basename of `argv[1]`
